title: autopilot.py runner start launches a headless sprint run and runner-status reports it
goal: New _tools/autopilot.py: 'runner start SP [--landed K]' makes or reuses the worktree .claude/worktrees/runner-<SP> at origin/main (a clean one is fast-forwarded, a dirty one is refused, naming its files) and runs claude -p '/kb-sprint run SP --headless --landed K' there with --output-format stream-json --verbose, --settings <that worktree's .claude/settings.json> and --plugin-dir for each plugin the project loads, passed explicitly; no --permission-mode or --dangerously-skip-permissions flag (the project's allow rules govern the run). The stream is written line by line to _cache/autopilot/<SP>/<UTC stamp>.jsonl; the runner ends the child on the first system compact_boundary event and records exit cause compaction, else landed-limit, sprint-done, blocked or error from the run's own final result and exit code, in _cache/autopilot/<SP>/status.json together with the start ref. 'runner-status SP' prints, in under 1000 characters, the landed items (done commits with KB-Work for the sprint's items since the start ref), gates the run added or left open on sprint items, bugs filed since the start ref, and the exit cause; it exits 1 when no run was recorded. Tests named autopilot_runner_* plant a fake claude that prints a recorded-shape stream (with and without a compact_boundary) and see the stream kept, the child ended at compaction, the status file and runner-status's length and content; a planted runner-status that prints the raw stream fails the length test. Any allow rule a headless run of /kb-sprint run needs that .claude/settings.json lacks is listed in the item's notes with its exact text for the operator, not added.

notes: Allow rules a headless "/kb-sprint run" needs that .claude/settings.json (permissions.allow) lacks, for the operator to add or refuse; none was added. The run passes no permission flag, so a command with no rule is refused. Already allowed: every python3 _tools/backlog.py command (claim, land, done, horizon, next, held, gate, answer), tests.py, stress_test.py, rag.py, check.py, selfdoc.py section, lint.py. Missing, as Bash rules (the PowerShell mirror of each is PowerShell(<same text>) for a Windows host): "Bash(python3 _tools/kbgit.py *)" (the claim sync kbgit.py sync --push, workers: kbgit.py fix --check, check-trailers); "Bash(python3 _tools/selfdoc.py stale *)" (workers); "Bash(git fetch *)"; "Bash(git status *)"; "Bash(git log *)"; "Bash(git show *)"; "Bash(git diff *)"; "Bash(git add *)"; "Bash(git commit *)"; "Bash(git rebase *)"; "Bash(git merge-base *)"; "Bash(git checkout *)"; "Bash(git branch *)"; "Bash(git cherry *)"; "Bash(git worktree *)"; "Bash(git -C *)"; "Bash(glab mr view *)"; "Bash(glab mr merge *)" (the code/<id> merge request, SKILL.md run step 4). Missing, as tool rules: "Agent" (the kb-worker subagents), "Edit" and "Write" (subagents change files in their worktrees), "SendMessage" (a subagent sent back to fix a gate or a refused done). For the manager session, not the runner: "Bash(python3 _tools/autopilot.py *)" (runner start, runner-status). Whether the harness already allows the read-only git commands (status, log, show, diff, merge-base, cherry) by default is not confirmed here; they are listed so a headless run does not depend on it.
